attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-pingds (import opsdir_adapter_pingds), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:pingds; depends on opsdir and opsdir-base-ds (and, through it, opsdir-adapter-ldap).
- adapter.py, ADAPTER:
  - kind product; applies via opsdir_base_ds.product.runs; products PingDS >=7.2,<9.
  - Required roles: subnet-ds, ds-ldaps-service, backup-target, ds-deployment-id, ds-deployment-password, ds-root-password, ds-tls-keystore.
  - The lineage's importers pingds/config, declared, access-log, rendered and schema, with reads_back; the lineage's config collectors.
  - Formats add ds/setup-*.sh.
- render.py: PINGDS product data; render_neutral (ldap/schema.ldif, ldap/dit.ldif, ds/dsconfig.batch, ds/acis.ldif); setup_scripts (ds/setup-<server>.sh).
- replication.py: check_replication (the target joins the source's deployment, and the replication path, through opsdir_base_ds.replication).
- logs.py LOGS, signals.py SIGNALS, versions.py VERSION_CHANGES.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["PingDS setup (run by the rendered ds/setup-<server>.sh scripts)", "PingDS ldapsearch (opsdir collect of cn=config over LDAPS)"]
attributes.purpose:
PingDS (ForgeRock DS lineage) product adapter: a thin layer on opsdir-base-ds for environments whose servers run PingDS >=7.2,<9.
- Renders the directory domain as the standard schema and tree LDIF, a dsconfig batch, ACI LDIF and per-server setup scripts that join the existing replication deployment.
- Reads back server configuration snapshots, the declared configuration, JSON access logs (consumers) and its own render.
- Collects cn=config over LDAPS with PingDS's ldapsearch.
- Declares the ds server role's listeners, logs, Prometheus signals and release changes, and the replication-continuity planner check.

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-pingfederate (import opsdir_adapter_pingfederate), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:pingfederate; depends on opsdir, opsdir-base-saml, opsdir-base-oidc and opsdir-format-terraform.
- Render targets: admin-api and terraform (default); terraform-imports and bulk-config (on request).
- Rendering: render.py, admin_api.py, admin_api_spec.py (vendored specs 12.1-13.1), terraform_target.py (provider schemas 1.8.1 and 1.10.0), bulk.py, connections.py, keypairs.py, discovery.py.
- Importers: pingfederate/bulk (importer.py; datastores, plugins, policies, oauth, messaging, generic resources held as is), pingfederate/node-files (nodes.py), pingfederate/cluster (discovery_import.py).
- Collector: bulk (collect.py).
- Schema prefix pingfed (schema.py).
- Seven planner checks (checks.py).
- Listeners, logs, proxy settings and version changes (versions.py); secrets withheld (withheld.py).
attributes.external_dependencies: ["PingFederate Admin API (/pf-admin-api/v1; bulk export read-only)", "Terraform provider pingidentity/pingfederate (1.8.1, 1.10.0)", "Ping pingfederate-go-client OpenAPI specs (vendored, Apache-2.0)", "JGroups discovery (TCPPING, NATIVE_S3_PING, DNS_PING)", "pyyaml (scripts/vendor-admin-api-specs.py only)", "Terraform CLI (scripts/vendor-provider-schemas.py; validation)"]
attributes.purpose:
PingFederate product adapter (PingFederate >=11,<14; server roles pf-engine and pf-admin).
- Renders each environment's configuration as Admin API requests checked against vendored version specs, as Terraform for the pingidentity/pingfederate provider, or, on request, as a bulk import document. It also renders JGroups cluster discovery and the standard SAML/OIDC documents at PingFederate's paths.
- Imports the Admin API bulk export (also collected live), the nodes' own files and the discovery file.
- Planner checks cover data stores, references, clustering, client and SMTP auth, service roles, JDBC drivers and version upgrades.

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-aws (import opsdir_adapter_aws), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:aws; depends on opsdir, opsdir-format-terraform, opsdir-format-cloudformation and pyyaml.
- Network: VPC/subnet data, security groups.
- Landing zone: plumbing (NAT, route tables, NACLs, peering, transit, VPN, flow logs), OIDC deployer roles, Identity Center permission sets, SCP guardrails.
- Compute: EC2 instances and Auto Scaling groups.
- Edge: NLBs, ALBs with WAFv2 and Shield, CloudFront (from the standard account in GovCloud), Route 53 and Resolver rules, VPC endpoints, Network Firewall allowlists.
- Data: RDS and Aurora, S3, EBS, DLM, AWS Backup.
- Identity: IAM roles.
- Security: CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Inspector, Config, Security Hub, Macie, suppressions.
- Observability: CloudWatch alarms and log groups, Synthetics canaries, Fluent Bit on EKS.
- Budgets.
- Importers: aws/terraform-state, aws/cli-inventory, aws/cloudformation, aws/regions, aws/quotas. Collectors for the first three.
- Planner checks: boundary, regulated placement, discovery availability, server inputs.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["terraform CLI (applies the rendered roots; terraform state pull for collect --terraform-dir)", "hashicorp/aws Terraform provider (~> 6.68)", "hashicorp/archive Terraform provider (~> 2.8; canary and Macie scheduler packaging)", "AWS CloudFormation (render target cloudformation; stacks read by aws/cloudformation)", "AWS CLI (aws-sm resolution, opsdir collect, aws/regions and aws/quotas runs)", "amazon.aws Ansible collection (secretsmanager_secret lookup via opsdir-adapter-ansible)", "Amazon CloudWatch agent and aws-for-fluent-bit (configured, not installed)", "AWS Load Balancer Controller (TargetGroupBinding for cluster gateways)", "cfn-lint (CloudFormation validation script and tests only)"]
attributes.purpose:
Amazon Web Services provider adapter (ciamCloudProvider aws, ciamCloudEnvironment public; a us-gov-* ciamRegion selects GovCloud (US) and the aws-us-gov partition).
- Renders an environment's infrastructure bindings as Terraform for hashicorp/aws, or as AWS CloudFormation translated from the same Terraform data; what CloudFormation can't express stays in a Terraform root.
- Reads them back from Terraform state, AWS CLI JSON and CloudFormation stacks, and collects all three read-only under the operator's AWS CLI login.
- Owns the aws-sm, aws-kms, aws-acm and s3 reference schemes and refuses AWS credential forms.
- Supplies the AWS access model, EKS IRSA and secret delivery, CloudWatch agent host files, and region and quota prerequisites.

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-format-terraform (import opsdir_format_terraform), registered via entry point opsdir.formats:hcl (format.FORMAT); depends on opsdir. Used by opsdir-adapter-aws, -azure, -gcp and -pingfederate.
- hcl.py: tf_name, TfBlock/tf_block, block, hcl, ref, jsonencoded, comment, tf_import, TfFile/hcl_file, written, data_block/data_value, blocks_of, mentions, as_text, ANCHOR/from_entry.
- hcl_reader.py: read_hcl, value_of.
- state.py: read_state.
- state_builder.py: tf_state, root_states.
- realized.py: realized.
- translate.py: roots, parse_ref/TfRef, partition, split_root, output_variable, no_native_note.
- placing.py: place_roots, carried_files.
- native.py: Native/Merge tables, read_root, resolver, translate, data_answer, placements, placements_document/placements_of, side_inputs.
attributes.purpose:
Terraform format library shared by the opsdir adapters. It knows HCL and Terraform, not any cloud provider or product.
- Writes HCL as data, laid out like terraform fmt, and reads back the subset it writes.
- Reads Terraform state (format 4, sensitive attributes dropped) and builds the state an apply would record from a render.
- Maps a block to the binding it realizes.
- Places a render in the roots of its keepers (origins, partition, placing).
- Runs the target-neutral engine that translates a Terraform root into another IaC language (AWS CloudFormation, Azure Bicep/ARM), keeping what has no native form in a side Terraform root.

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-kubernetes (import opsdir_adapter_kubernetes), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:kubernetes; depends on opsdir and pyyaml.
- Declares: scheme k8s-secret (with an Ansible kubernetes.core.k8s lookup), render targets external-secrets and csi, estate setting kubernetes-gateway-implementation, vocabulary ciamGatewayImplementation and importer kubernetes/workloads. No schema, required roles or planner checks.
- render.py: namespace, service accounts, network policies, ExternalSecrets, SecretProviderClasses, CSI sync pods, secrets-required.yaml.
- gateway.py: Gateway, HTTPRoutes, BackendTLSPolicy, backend CA and cookie stickiness per implementation (istio by default, envoy-gateway).
- workloads.py, gateway_import.py: the importer.
- kits.py, names.py: helpers and marks shared with the deployment-kit adapters.
- secrets.py: k8s-secret resolution.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["pyyaml", "kubectl (k8s-secret:// resolution)", "Ansible kubernetes.core collection (k8s lookup)", "Gateway API v1.6.1 standard channel", "Istio 1.31.1 (default gateway implementation)", "Envoy Gateway v1.9.2", "External Secrets Operator (external-secrets.io/v1)", "Secrets Store CSI driver (secrets-store.csi.x-k8s.io/v1)", "kustomize and kubeconform (validation only)"]
attributes.purpose: Kubernetes platform adapter. For environments that run workloads on Kubernetes it renders per-namespace kustomizations: the namespace with its pod-security level, service accounts annotated with the provider's workload identity, network policies from the deployment kits' or products' listeners, Secret delivery (render targets external-secrets and csi) and a secrets-required list. It also renders the in-cluster Gateway API gateway behind a cloud's front (Istio or Envoy Gateway), resolves k8s-secret:// references, and imports workloads, workload bindings, CronJobs and Gateways from manifests (kubernetes/workloads).

attributes.description:
Distribution opsdir-adapter-gcp (import opsdir_adapter_gcp), registered via entry point opsdir.adapters:gcp; depends on opsdir and opsdir-format-terraform.
- Network: Shared VPC network data; firewall rules by network tag, or a network firewall policy by secure tag; Private Service Connect; egress allowlists.
- Landing zone: plumbing (Cloud NAT, routes, peering, HA VPN), workload identity federation, org-policy guardrails, Assured Workloads, budgets.
- Compute: Compute Engine instances and regional managed instance groups.
- Edge: passthrough and Application load balancers with Cloud Armor, Cloud CDN and Cloud DNS.
- Data: Cloud SQL, buckets, disks, snapshot schedules, Backup and DR.
- Identity: service accounts and IAM members.
- Security: audit sinks, Security Command Center, Compliance Manager, mute rules, Sensitive Data Protection.
- Observability: alert policies, log buckets and sinks, uptime checks, synthetic monitors.
- Importers: gcp/terraform-state, gcp/cli-inventory, gcp/regions, gcp/quotas, gcp/frameworks.
- Collectors: cli-inventory, terraform-state.
- Planner checks: priorities, boundary, regulated placement, server inputs, discovery cadence.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["terraform CLI (applies the rendered roots; terraform state pull for collect --terraform-dir)", "hashicorp/google Terraform provider (~> 8.6)", "hashicorp/archive Terraform provider (~> 2.8; synthetic monitor source packaging)", "gcloud CLI (gcp-sm resolution, opsdir collect, gcp/regions, gcp/quotas and gcp/frameworks runs, Policy Troubleshooter in access/evaluate.sh)", "Google Cloud Ops Agent (configured, not installed)"]
attributes.purpose:
Google Cloud provider adapter (ciamCloudProvider gcp, ciamCloudEnvironment public).
- Renders an environment's infrastructure bindings as Terraform for hashicorp/google, in platform, landing-zone and per-keeper roots.
- Reads them back from Terraform state and from Cloud Asset Inventory and gcloud JSON, and collects both read-only under the operator's gcloud login.
- Owns the gcp-sm, gcp-kms, gcp-cert and gs reference schemes (gcp-sm resolved with gcloud) and refuses Google Cloud credential forms.
- Supplies the Google Cloud access model, GKE workload identity and secret delivery, Ops Agent host files, region, quota and compliance-framework prerequisites, and Assured Workloads boundary checks.

attributes.name: _allowlist
attributes.purpose: Finding for one external allowlist: role unbound (blocker), already covered (ok), or dated request (action + request)

attributes.name: check_data_stores
attributes.purpose: Planner check: data stores with withheld credentials but no credential role, or needing roles the target doesn't bind, are blockers; a fixed host or an LDAP store without TLS is an action; an ok line when every store is fine; nothing when there are no data stores

attributes.name: check_jobs
attributes.purpose: Planner check over the jobs that apply in the source (core environment.applies_in): those also applying in the target are checked (no servers of their role, roles nobody binds -> blockers; no owner / nowhere to run -> actions); those that don't apply in the target are an action each (it won't run there; scope it too if it should).

attributes.name: check_hosts
attributes.purpose: Planner check: per baseline applying in the source or target, truststore certificates the record lacks and pinned hosts; roles the target runs (and the source too) with no baseline applying in the target; weaker/less spread target compute groups (with fixes).

attributes.name: check_workloads
attributes.purpose: Planner check: blockers for a workload the source runs on Kubernetes that the target neither runs there (workload binding) nor has servers of its role, a target workload binding without its cluster, identity or Secret-filling roles neither environment binds; actions for a role moving servers<->Kubernetes (host baseline into the image, or back) and privileged workloads; ok line otherwise.

attributes.name: check_services
attributes.purpose: Planner check: target names missing from a service's allowed domains, roles a service or sender uses that nobody binds, target sending identities without DKIM/SPF or for another domain are blockers; services without owner, weaker DMARC, senders without bounce handling are actions.

attributes.name: check_alerts
attributes.purpose: Planner check: alert rules whose delivering role, and canaries whose checked service or credential roles, neither environment binds are blockers; alert rules without a runbook or owner and canaries feeding no alert rule are actions; an ok line otherwise

attributes.name: check_logs
attributes.purpose: Planner check: a route whose destination role neither environment binds, or whose target destination keeps logs fewer days than the route's obligation (0 = indefinite meets any), is a blocker (the latter with a fix setting the target destination's ciamRetentionDays); unknown target retention, a source already short, and legal-hold logs are actions; an ok line otherwise.

attributes.name: check_egress
attributes.purpose: Planner check: partner-ingress allowlists of the target's egress binding must name a fixed public address the routes use (actions dated by cutover).

attributes.name: check_sites
attributes.purpose: Planner check: required outside sites the target's egress proxy/firewall doesn't allow (an action for its owner, and a request per site, topic network, to the party ciamManagedBy names when one is recorded: any brand of proxy or a hub firewall, no file format needed); firewalls with domain rules no default route sends egress through.

attributes.name: kept_by
attributes.purpose: Name of who keeps a binding the stack doesn't (the ciamManagedBy party's RDN, else its DN).

attributes.name: object_store_rows
attributes.purpose: The object-stores report (OBJECT_STORE_HEADERS): one row per object store of every environment (backup targets among them), sorted by environment and role: environment, role, kind, location, versioning, immutability (mode and days), encrypted by, lifecycle, public blocked, replica, retention days, kept by

attributes.name: coverage
attributes.purpose: What environment m's audit trails cover together: events recorded (AUDIT_EVENTS order), any all-regions, the best integrity grade (integrity: UNPROTECTED 0 / UNLOCKED 1 / PROTECTED 2), the longest destination retention (0 = forever, None unknown)

attributes.name: audit_rows
attributes.purpose: audit-trails report: one row per trail of every environment: scope, events, all regions, integrity (validated / locked immutable store / unlocked immutable store / no / ''), destination role, retention days (forever), keeper (platform unless ciamManagedBy)

attributes.name: service_coverage
attributes.purpose: What environment m's services (usually of one kind) give together (SecurityCoverage): areas watched, frameworks and provider baselines assessed, organization scope, all regions, findings routed, longest records kept (own ciamRetentionDays or findings destination's).

attributes.name: security_rows
attributes.purpose: Report security-services: one row per security service of every environment (kind, scope, all regions, areas, standards + baselines, findings role, keep days, keeper).

attributes.name: budget_rows
attributes.purpose: Report budgets: one row per budget of every environment: amount+currency, period, alert thresholds spent/forecast, alert role, keeper

attributes.name: discovery_rows
attributes.purpose: Report data-discovery: one row per data discovery service of every environment (stores examined, own data types by name, rescan days, findings to, results to, kept by)

attributes.name: managed_by
attributes.purpose: The party entry an entry's ciamManagedBy names, or None when it names none or the record has no such entry (core directory.follow): who keeps the entry when the stack doesn't. Shared by every domain that asks who keeps a binding (U14-09).

attributes.name: managed_by_name
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "e", "type": "Entry", "required": true}, {"name": "default", "type": "str | None", "description": "the name when no party entry is named", "required": false}]
attributes.purpose: The name of who keeps an entry as reports and findings show it: the RDN value of the party its ciamManagedBy names (managed_by), else default. Callers pass 'platform', '?', or the DN named.

attributes.name: all_clear
attributes.purpose: A check's parts (Findings) merged (merge_findings), with ok_line, the check's one line saying all it looked at holds, added to what is fine when none of the parts is a blocker or an action. The shared end of the domain checks (U14-11).

attributes.name: each_checked
attributes.purpose: A check over items: no findings when there are none; else judge(item) (Findings) for each, merged, with ok_line added when nothing is a blocker or an action (all_clear).

attributes.name: retention_days
attributes.purpose: How many days a binding keeps what it is sent (ciamRetentionDays as an int; INDEFINITE, 0, means forever), or None when the binding is None or records none. Shared by the audit, logs and security reports and checks (U14-12).

attributes.name: longest_retention
attributes.purpose: The longest of several retentions (retention_days values): INDEFINITE when any keeps forever, else the most days; None when none is recorded.

attributes.name: yes_no
attributes.purpose: A report's cell for a boolean attribute of an entry: 'yes' for TRUE, 'no' for FALSE, '' when not recorded.
